# IDM-MCP Core ⇄ Stream-Downloader — every line, side by side

This document places **every line** of the original private MCP (`C:\Development\IDM`, IDM-MCP Core 0.3.1) beside the corresponding line of **Stream-Downloader** 1.0.0, its simplified, fully decoupled mirror of the video downloader by Angela López Mendoza. Every removal, change and addition carries its reason.

It is generated, never hand-edited: `python tools/generate_comparison.py` writes it (and `COMPARISON.html`, the same content for comfortable reading), and `tests/verify_comparison.py` proves it is complete and current. Generation refuses to run if any file of either project is unaccounted for.

Input fingerprint: `1e00f1582cc78a6f97455b6276927b02275402810e2fbe394e12bc3edade8bf7` — 45 IDM files and 44 Stream-Downloader files.

## How to read it

| Mark | Meaning |
| :-: | --- |
| `=` | identical line |
| `≈` | same line after the systematic rename (IdmMcp → StreamDownloader, idm_* → stream_*, own folders and markers) |
| `✎` | the line was changed; the last column says why |
| `−` | IDM line with no counterpart: removed, and why |
| `+` | Stream-Downloader line with no counterpart: added, and why |

| 40 | <code>IDM-MCP should be a local, Windows-only Model Context Protocol (MCP) service that safely turns an &#42;&#42;authorized, technically downloadable resource&#42;&#42; into a durable job, submits it to the installed IDM through Tonec's documented COM API, and independently verifies the resulting file.</code> | − |  |  | IDM's archived design proposals; history, not part of the mirror. |

| 42 | <code>The requested literal guarantee—“every link from every site, always downloaded in any requested quality/container”—cannot be implemented honestly by IDM, an MCP server, or any other downloader. A URL may identify an HTML page rather than a media file; a requested rendition may not exist; a signed media URL may expire; a stream may be encrypted/DRM-protected; a platform may prohibit automated downloading; a server, network, disk, account, or IDM may fail. YouTube in particular prohibits automated access and downloading except where the service or the relevant rights holders expressly authorize it. Owning an IDM license licenses IDM; it does not grant rights to third-party content or override a site's terms.</code> | − |  |  | IDM's archived design proposals; history, not part of the mirror. |

| 46 | <code>&gt; While the Windows account, Agent, and durable state store remain available, every accepted request receives an idempotent job and is driven toward a truthful terminal state. Unsupported, protected, forbidden, unavailable, ambiguous, and failed cases are reported explicitly—never disguised as success and never silently substituted.</code> | − |  |  | IDM's archived design proposals; history, not part of the mirror. |

| 334 | <code>There is an essential integration gap: Tonec documents the panel as a browser-to-IDM workflow, while the public COM API accepts an already resolved download URL and does not expose “resolve this watch page” or “list panel renditions.” Seeing a panel label does not by itself give IDM-MCP the direct URL needed for &#96;SendLinkToIDM2&#96;. The design will not bridge that gap by reading private extension messages or hidden storage. A supported browser adapter must prove one of two fully visible/documented paths: (a) the UI exposes an authorized direct resource that can be vaulted and submitted through COM, or (b) clicking the official panel opens a visible IDM dialog where the exact service-owned staging path and frozen filename can be set and verified before start.
